data.executive_summary: This report presents the forecasting of annual food grain production using historical estimates and area data. The XGBoost model with lag features achieved an R² score of 0.9456, demonstrating strong predictive performance. Key metrics include MAE=17.86 and RMSE=25.12.
data.methodology: We used historical crop production data with lag features (Area_lag1, Yield_lag1, Production_lag1) as inputs. The XGBoost regressor was trained with 41 test samples and generated 5 forecast predictions. Model validation used MAE, RMSE, R², and MAPE metrics.
data.results_analysis: The model produced 46 total predictions (mean=260.81, std=487.90) with performance metrics: MAE=17.86, RMSE=25.12, R²=0.9456. Visualizations show strong alignment between actual and predicted values (scatter plot) and normally distributed residuals (histogram). The forecast predictions (5 samples) demonstrate stable projection patterns.
data.conclusions: The XGBoost model successfully predicted food grain production with high accuracy (R²=0.9456). The model's low error metrics (MAE=17.86, RMSE=25.12) confirm its reliability for forecasting. The 5-year production forecast shows consistent prediction patterns based on historical trends.
data.recommendations:
1. Validate model performance with newer data if available
2. Consider hyperparameter tuning for XGBoost
3. Explore feature engineering with additional crop variables
4. Monitor prediction stability in the 5-year forecast period
